title: Open Redirect via KC_REDIRECT Cookie in KeycloakAuthenticationSuccessHandler
analysis:
Data path trace:
- Source: Untrusted user input enters through the HTTP request cookie `KC_REDIRECT` retrieved via `KeycloakCookieBasedRedirect.getRedirectUrlFromCookie(request)` at line 52. Furthermore, in `KeycloakAuthenticationEntryPoint.commenceLoginRedirect`, the unauthenticated request URI (`request.getRequestURI()`) is stored directly into the `KC_REDIRECT` cookie without validation.
- Sanitization/Validation: There is no validation, URL parsing, or domain allowlisting performed on `location`. Any arbitrary URL (including external URLs or protocol-relative URLs like `//attacker.com`) is accepted as-is.
- Sink: `response.sendRedirect(location)` at line 60.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
1. An attacker tricks an unauthenticated user into clicking a link to the application:
   `https://victim-app.example.com//attacker.example.com/login`
2. `KeycloakAuthenticationEntryPoint` stores the request URI `//attacker.example.com/login` into the `KC_REDIRECT` cookie and redirects the user to Keycloak for authentication.
3. After the user successfully authenticates, Keycloak redirects back to `victim-app.example.com`.
4. `KeycloakAuthenticationSuccessHandler.onAuthenticationSuccess` reads `KC_REDIRECT` (`//attacker.example.com/login`) and executes `response.sendRedirect("//attacker.example.com/login")`.
5. The user's browser is immediately redirected to `https://attacker.example.com/login`, enabling phishing or credential theft.
Alternatively, an attacker can directly set the cookie in a request:
```http
GET /login/oauth2/code/keycloak?state=...&code=... HTTP/1.1
Host: victim-app.example.com
Cookie: KC_REDIRECT=https://attacker.example.com/phish
```
The handler directly redirects the victim to `https://attacker.example.com/phish`.
vuln_type: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')
